title: HMMER web server: 2026 update.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: The web server landing page returns HTTP 200 (a 2.7 KB HTML page for a JavaScript app); a guessed API root /api/v1/ returned 404. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles request timed out once and was not retried; Europe PMC flags the paper hasSuppl=N. The data availability statement only gives the server and software URLs. There is no downloadable dataset or table.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the server: a React interface rebuilt from scratch, a JSON API, horizontal scaling, and updated target databases. The only text-mined accession (HG009116) is incidental, not a dataset deposit.

a1_downloadable.note: This is a software and web-service update paper. No dataset is deposited; the server runs searches on demand and is free with no login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No table and no label column exist. Any target (for example, a domain hit or E-value, the HMMER score for how likely a match is by chance) would have to be generated by running HMMER yourself.

a3_inputs_present.note: No input data comes with the paper; the protein sequence databases it searches belong to other resources (UniProt, Pfam).

a5_enough_rows.note: No rows: no dataset accompanies the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any label built from server output would be HMMER's own computed prediction (profile HMM, a statistical model of a protein family, scores and hits). Training on it would only distil HMMER (circular).

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (would only apply if labels were generated by running HMMER)

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the paper releases a web service, not a measured dataset.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequences to predict which protein family domains they contain, imitating a profile-matching search tool.
plain_idea.train_on: Protein sequences that we would have to label ourselves by running the search tool; the paper provides no examples (count unknown).
plain_idea.predict: Family or domain assignments. The true answer would be the search tool's own computed output, not a lab measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Fast embedding-based alternatives to profile search are of some interest, but this paper adds no data for that; existing tools such as NEAR (which the paper cites) already address it.

ml_idea: None from this paper. Distilling HMMER or Pfam domain calls into a protein language model head is possible from Pfam or InterPro directly, but it is circular (labels come from HMMER) and already explored.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: there is no dataset to build a table from.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check the data availability statement: it lists only the server and software URLs, so there is no dataset (already done).

verdict_reason: Software and web-server update paper with no deposited dataset or label column (fails A1, A2 and A5). Any label made with the server would be HMMER's own computed output (fails A8, circular). Existing-model searches were skipped because Part A failed.
